goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication.rationale: In the shown portion of `GroupResource.addChild`, the only permission enforcement visible is `auth.groups().requireManage(group)` on the *target parent* group, and the diff does not add any check on the referenced existing child when `rep.getId() != null` (it only changes `GroupModel child = null` to `GroupModel child;`). This PR also introduces per-group fine-grained permissions in V2 (`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(GroupModel)` / `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` based on group-scoped permissions), which makes it plausible that a caller could have MANAGE/MANAGE_MEMBERS on parent P without any rights on child C; if `addChild` allows re-parenting C under P without validating rights on C, that creates a privilege-escalation path consistent with the finding (via hierarchy-based checks like `UserPermissions.canManageByGroup(...)` using `root.groups()::canManageMembers`). However, the full `addChild` method body is not included in the diff, so it cannot be conclusively verified that no later check exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses findByType("Groups"), but per-group resources are created without a type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121), and it adds resource.getId() instead of the group id (V1 uses the name), so user search and count get filtered by a bogus id (zero results or zero count with all-groups view-members) and per-group grants are never included.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:103 — View-members and manage-members search tests pass only because the broken group-id filter comes back empty and the per-user canView post-filter takes over; they never check /users/count, pagination or all-groups view-members, so the broken query path goes green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a likely broken “group ids with view permission” path: `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, and also calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`. However `hasPermission` looks up resources by **name** (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`), and `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` indicates group resources are named by the actual **group id** (used as the resource name). Passing/storing the authorization resource internal id instead of the Keycloak group id means the lookup will miss, permissions won’t be recognized, and the returned set will often be empty. That empty/incorrect set is then used by `UsersResource.getUsersCount(..., auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission())` and by user search via `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`, potentially breaking filtering/count behavior. The test file indeed does not cover `/users/count` or pagination, so it could miss this regression.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `UserPermissionsV2` to allow user access via group-chain permissions: `canView(UserModel)` now returns `hasPermission(... VIEW, MANAGE) || canViewByGroup(user)` and `canManage(UserModel)` similarly ORs with `canManageByGroup(user)`. This is reinforced by updated Javadocs in `UserPermissionEvaluator` describing view/manage being granted via `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS` on ancestor groups, and by the new test `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest#testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` validating this behavior. The finding’s claim about a user-specific permission that “denies” being overridden is not supported by the diff (the code checks for presence of granted scopes, not an explicit deny concept).

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:250 — init() returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms that enabled V2 before this change never get the "Groups" resource or the new scopes; getResourceTypeResource then returns null and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission:147 calls findByResource(server, null), and creating group permissions fails with "No scopes found".

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on behavior in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` (early return when admin-permissions client exists) and the behavior of `getResourceTypeResource()`, but neither `init()` nor `getResourceTypeResource()` appear in the provided diff. From the diff alone we can only see that a new GROUPS `ResourceType` and scopes were added to the schema map, and that `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` does not null-check the result of `getResourceTypeResource()`. The claimed broken upgrade path (existing realms missing the new Groups resource/scopes leading to `findByResource(server, null)` and "No scopes found") is not directly verifiable from the diff shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:74 — The removal listener is now registered only for V1, so with V2 deleting a group (or user or client) leaves its FGAP V2 per-group resource and permissions orphaned in the admin-permissions client.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show the removal listener being “registered only for V1”. It is now registered only when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled (the same condition previously checked inside `onEvent`), so behavior is effectively equivalent from what’s shown. Also, the diff provides no evidence that V2 runs with the feature disabled or that V2 deletions would therefore skip cleanup and orphan resources; that V1/V2 linkage is not established in the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java:36 — Giving the test admin QUERY_GROUPS hides that V2 canList() (QUERY_GROUPS or all-groups view/manage only) returns 403 on GET /groups for admins who hold only per-group view permissions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS` to the test admin in `RealmAdminPermissionsConfig` (lines around 36). At the same time, `GroupPermissions.canList()` was tightened to `root.hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()` and `GroupPermissionsV2.canView()` only grants global view via admin roles or an *all-groups* VIEW/MANAGE permission (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`), not via per-group VIEW permissions.
